To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the usability of technical devices is influenced by the aesthetic design of the devices, and the aesthetic design is influenced by the usability of technical systems.
the design of a technical system has a strong impact on the emotional reactions and the overall appraisal of the user.
the design of a technical product affects the user’s experience and that the experience of the user is a crucial factor for the success of the design.
In summary, our research is concerned with
human–technology interaction in a broad sense and aims at providing a theoretical foundation for the study of human–technology experience.
the question of how people experience technology. We argue that this question cannot be answered solely by considering instrumental aspects of technology.
the role of usability, aesthetics and emotion in human–technology interactions and with the interplay of the three aspects.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
usability is not everything.
usability is an important aspect of user experience, but not the only one.
the CUE-Model is the first model of user experience that is empirically validated and that integrates the important aspects of human-technology interaction.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that emotions and aesthetic experiences play a central role in the interaction with technology.
we have to consider the emotional aspects of human–computer interaction.
usability, aesthetics and emotions are important aspects for the design of interactive systems.
The main takeaway from our work is that
usability is a necessary but not sufficient condition for user experience.
the design and evaluation of human–technology systems should not be restricted to instrumental aspects but also consider non-instrumental aspects such as aesthetics and emotions.
usability, aesthetics and emotions are not separate aspects of human– technology interaction, but rather interrelated components of user experience that should be considered in concert.
